content: 1. Erythromycin lactobionate and buprenorphine buccal both prolong the QTc interval. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implants by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Patients on buprenorphine subdermal implants who require CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored for signs of overmedication. If dose adjustment of the CYP3A4 inhibitor is not possible, implant removal may be necessary, and the patient should be transitioned to a buprenorphine dosage form that allows dose adjustments. 3. Erythromycin lactobionate and buprenorphine subdermal implants both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Erythromycin lactobionate and buprenorphine transdermal both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Patients transitioning to buprenorphine long-acting injection from transmucosal buprenorphine coadministered with CYP3A4 inhibitors should be monitored to ensure adequate plasma levels of buprenorphine. 6. Erythromycin lactobionate and buprenorphine long-acting injection both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 9. Butalbital decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 10. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cabozantinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Calcium carbonate increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 14. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of capivasertib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Reduce the capivasertib dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 15. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, while erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Monitor plasma levels closely if used concomitantly. 16. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of cefdinir through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 17. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of cefditoren through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 18. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of cefoxitin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 19. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of cefpodoxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 20. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of ceftriaxone through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 21. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the effects of cefuroxime through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 22. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. Increase the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. 23. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Ceritinib and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 25. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of erythromycin lactobionate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Chlorpromazine and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 28. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the efficacy of the cholera vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration of the cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may be active against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 29. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Dose reduction to 50 mg twice daily should be considered. 30. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 31. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cinacalcet by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Ciprofloxacin and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of ciprofloxacin with drugs known to prolong the QT interval could increase the risk of torsade de pointes in predisposed patients; however, this is less likely with ciprofloxacin than with other quinolones. 33. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Citalopram and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 35. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 36. Clindamycin and erythromycin lactobionate may decrease the effects of each other through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 37. Clindamycin topical and erythromycin lactobionate may decrease the effects of each other through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 38. Clomipramine and erythromycin lactobionate both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 39. Erythromycin lactobionate decreases the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which reduces clopidogrel bioactivation. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 40. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of clozapine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 41. Cobicistat and erythromycin lactobionate both increase the levels of each other by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 42. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 43. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of colchicine by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is necessary, decrease the colchicine dose or frequency as recommended in prescribing information. Use of colchicine with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 44. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 45. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. 46. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cortisone by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 47. Crizotinib increases the levels of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. 49. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 50. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 51. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification or close monitoring is advised. 52. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the levels or effects of dactinomycin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Erythromycin lactobionate increases the effects of dalteparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 54. Danazol increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown.
